summary: Lando Norris plants McLaren on pole at the treacherous new Madrid circuit with a masterful qualifying lap, positioning himself to steal another victory despite Mercedes and Red Bull breathing down his neck in a track where overtaking proves brutally difficult. George Russell warns the high-risk layout could shuffle the entire field come race day, with tight margins and unforgiving barriers threatening to punish any driver who loses concentration on the unfamiliar asphalt. A dominant finish would extend Norris' championship charge and signal McLaren's genuine threat to Red Bull's dominance, while any mechanical failure or collision could hand Verstappen or Antonelli an unexpected opening in the standings.
